Given that the HKMA’s operations and backup data centre account for a major portion of the institution’s overall energy consumption, both data centres have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for Existing Data Centres, achieving optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE)13. In 2023, the HKMA’s two data centres were awarded “Gold” and “Platinum” ratings respectively under the assessment guidelines “BEAM Plus Existing Data Centres” issued in 2021; the HKMA is the first and only entity in Hong Kong to receive these ratings. Enhancing the energy efficiency of the two data centres has always been a focus of the Technology Division. To this end, the division adopted green design in renovation works and employed energy-efficient best practices to lower PUE and achieve related targets, including 24-hour monitoring of the data centres’ environmental facilities and continuous enhancements to environmental factors such as airflow and temperature settings. With the Technology Division continuously improving energy use in the data centres, the HKMA commissioned external consultants in December 2021 to conduct a review to comprehensively evaluate the green performance of the data centres and formulate recommendations to further enhance performance in various aspects. The relevant studies were completed in mid-2022. Shortly after the completion of the studies, the HKMA started preparing to obtain the “Green Data Centre” qualification under the BEAM Plus certification scheme. The certification process is very comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout the entire year of 2023, the Technology Division introduced enhancements based on the recommendations in the consultant’s report, upgrading energy performance as well as healthier elements of the working environment within the data centres.

Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency has undertaken an independent verification of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority’s (“HKMA”) 2023 environmental dataset (“2023 Dataset”). The 2023 Dataset includes total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions, business air travel GHG emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste) for 2023, their respective intensity, and the change compared to 2015 levels. Moreover, the 2023 Dataset also includes the amount of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and the change compared to the levels when the HKMA started introducing the Food Waste Recycling Programme in November 2022. The HKMA’s GHG emission data was prepared based on the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (“GHG Protocol”) jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covers relevant data for the period from January 1, 2023 to December 31, 2023, and also covers relevant data for the period from January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2015 used for annual performance comparison (excluding food waste). The verification scope covers a total of five office and warehouse assets, of which four offices are located at: 1) Two International Finance Centre; 2) Hopewell Centre; 3) Pacific Place Phase One; 4) Kowloon Trading Hub; and the warehouse is located at 5) Lok Sing Industrial Building, Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Dataset and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanisms. Within the verification scope, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency examined representative sample data and supporting evidence selected from the five assets. This verification engagement was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information,” issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were specifically designed to form opinions and conclusions to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification processes were established as required by the GHG Protocol. The verification processes tested the completeness and accuracy of data by tracing selected sample data back to its source, and also reviewed the underlying processes of data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and performed reliability testing. The verification processes also included verifying domestic data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with proxies responsible for preparing the 2023 Dataset, and selecting representative data and information for examination. Relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of the information. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team has not participated in the preparation processes of the 2023 Dataset. Based on the results of this verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the 2023 Dataset and concludes that: the 2023 Dataset is materially accurate and reliable; and the HKMA’s headline data collection mechanisms are strong. Sham Siu Yan Audit Manager Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency April 2024

The threat posed by climate change is imminent, making it imperative to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization confirmed that 2024 was the hottest year on record, and also the first year in which global temperatures exceeded the critical threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Meanwhile, although global GHG emissions eased slightly during the COVID-19 pandemic, they have recently reached new highs, underscoring the inadequacy of current measures to mitigate climate change. In the process of combating global warming, the materialisation of climate-related risks is set to become heightened, with unpredictable impacts on the economy and financial market. Moreover, current geopolitical tensions, the increasing fragmentation of the global economic landscape, growing concerns over energy security, and an uncertain economic outlook all present greater challenges for countries in combating climate change. The transformation towards a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained funding support. Around the world, Asia faces the most severe transition challenges. As highlighted by the World Economic Forum, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth but also the region most vulnerable to climate change. Therefore, Asia plays a key role in whether the world can successfully achieve its net-zero target. As a leading international finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong needs to strengthen its leading role and fully leverage the power of finance to support and foster regional transformation. To this end, the HKMA announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" last year, setting out our vision and roadmap for progressively integrating sustainability into the core of the financial system. Our work focuses on enhancing the banking sector's ability to manage climate-related risks on one hand, and assisting the industry in seizing related new opportunities on the other. At the same time, we are leading by example. The HKMA’s sustainability work encompasses four key areas: supporting the banking sector towards net-zero, investing in a sustainable future, fostering net-zero financing, and promoting more inclusive sustainable development. The banking system plays a key role in the net-zero transition of Hong Kong and Asia, yet banks themselves face significant risks during this transition. Under the "Action Plan", we have set ambitious targets, requiring all banks to strive to achieve net-zero in their own operations by 2030 or before, and net-zero in their financing by 2050 or before. We also require all banks to enhance disclosure of climate-related risks and opportunities. While continuing to strengthen banks' climate risk management, we have also provided guidelines for banks’ transition planning to help them upgrade their capacity to manage the transition and better manage related risks. We are also undertaking preparatory work with relevant stakeholders to align Hong Kong's sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, aiming to further increase transparency in related activities within the industry. Additionally, we are making enhancements to the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance introduced in May last year by incorporating more sustainable activities (including transition activities). We expect that by providing clear criteria, we can guide more funding towards sustainable and transition-related projects. Climate change brings significant physical and transition risks that may impact the long-term financial performance and worth of Exchange Fund investment projects. Yet at the same time, it also presents opportunities for the Exchange Fund to generate growth and drive positive impact. Our experience demonstrates that investment return and positive sustainable impact can be coordinated without conflict. In light of this, we are committed to striving for net-zero in the Exchange Fund portfolio by 2050 or before, and have promised in the "Action Plan" to support Asia's climate transition through Exchange Fund investments. Currently, sustainable investments already account for more than 10% of the portfolio. To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and the International Finance Corporation last November to accelerate the low-carbon economic transition in Asia through co-investment. Furthermore, we published the inaugural "HKMA ESG Expectations" document last September to further encourage fund managers to proactively exercise asset ownership and adopt sound sustainable investment practices. Financing is particularly important for accelerating the regional transition. As an international finance hub and the premier venue for arranging international sustainable bonds for Asian issuers (including Mainland provincial and municipal governments), Hong Kong plays a vital role in channelling capital to accelerate regional transformation. The "Action Plan" outlines the vision of developing Hong Kong into the region's preferred sustainable financing platform and the goal of fostering sustainable finance innovation. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" to foster green bond innovation (including the offering of the first multi-currency Digital Bond globally last February), to expanding the coverage of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" to include transition financing instruments last May, and to the introduction of the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme" last November, we have been committed to encouraging regional issuers to utilise Hong Kong's financial platform to raise the funding required for decarbonisation and transition. Achieving a sound transition requires not only capital and innovation but also the support of an inclusive and accessible sustainable development system. This includes reliable sustainability dataset, highly transparent information disclosure, and industry talent equipped with relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, we have promised in the "Action Plan" to support the promotion of high-quality and full sustainable disclosure, and to strive to bridge the gap in sustainable finance talent and knowledge in the region. We have made good progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainable disclosure, particularly by providing convenient and user-friendly climate disclosure templates to foster sustainable disclosure by small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). We also introduced the "Green and Sustainable Finance" Professional Level module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for banking professionals last November to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local bank staff. Furthermore, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held last February and other activities, we have engaged various sectors in discussions on sustainable development, thereby fostering co-operation and innovation. Internally, the HKMA is committed to ensuring our operating processes align with our sustainability vision. We have promised in the "Action Plan" to achieve net-zero in our own operations by 2030 or before, bringing forward our original commitment by 20 years. Moreover, in accordance with the roadmap promulgated by the government, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainable disclosure standards. We started adopting electric vehicles in 2024 and incorporated low carbon emission as a selection factor in our procurement processes. Meanwhile, we continue to improve efficiency through digitalising, cultivate a culture of sustainability within the organisation, and motivate staff to actively participate in sustainability initiatives. Multilateral co-operation has always been the cornerstone of the global response to climate change, but the reshaping of the international landscape and drastic changes in geopolitical situations have added variables to global climate action. That said, climate change is an undeniable fact that is progressively intensifying. In the work of combating climate change, the current situation does not allow for any relaxation. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help mitigate the impact of climate risk on Hong Kong's financial system and bring us opportunities in the process. Looking ahead to 2025, we will continue to forge ahead, strive to advance sustainability work, and deepen relationships with like-minded partners. Despite facing severe challenges, we will remain committed, as always, to supporting Hong Kong, Asia, and other regions in building a sustainable future.

Climate change is a major challenge confronting our generation. As an international financial centre and a regional sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development in Asia and globally. In October 2024, the HKMA announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), which sets out the HKMA’s vision in this area, including our future direction, the timeline for achieving various targets, and how we expect the industry to work together to advance related efforts. The HKMA plans to strengthen the ability of Hong Kong’s financial sector and the HKMA itself to combat climate change risks, and to foster Asia’s transformation towards a more sustainable economy, through formulating strategic policies, strengthening regulatory co-operation, and upgrading internal operations. Through active participation in international and regional discussions, the HKMA also strives to exert influence and participate in the formulation of green and sustainable finance policies and standards at both regional and global levels. As a banking sector regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the climate resilience of the banking sector and supporting banks in remaining safe and sound during their transition to net-zero. Our key priorities for 2025 include: - Launching a new round of thematic reviews on banks’ climate risk management practices and conducting a third round of consultation sessions to assess banks’ implementation of relevant supervisory requirements issued by the HKMA, and to further strengthen banks’ climate risk management capabilities; - Refining the work on incorporating climate risk stress testing into the HKMA’s supervisor-led stress-tested framework; - Continued advancement of work to integrate climate factors into the HKMA’s supervisory review process; - Commencing preparatory work for formulating relevant supervisory requirements regarding the implementation by local banks of the Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks and the International Financial Reporting Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) to be issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision; - Completing the compilation of the new module GS-2 of the Supervisory Policy Manual to provide guidelines to banks on transition planning; and - Sharing good practices with the industry on climate risk management and the application of green fintech. Beyond its role as a banking sector regulator, the HKMA also acts as a facilitator, committed to fostering the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in providing financing for the transition. We have published Phase 1 of the "Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Taxonomy", providing the industry with a derivative to identify green and sustainable economic activities and facilitate related funding flows. The HKMA has commenced work on Phase 2 of the Taxonomy to expand its coverage, including adding transition elements, increasing green economic activities, and incorporating climate change adaptation objectives. Moreover, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will organise another green fintech event in 2025 to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks. Hong Kong is well-positioned to support regional sustainable financing needs. To strengthen this role, we will continue to assist the government in implementing the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme", whose expanded scope will cover sustainable projects such as social responsibility projects. This will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and serve as a demonstration for other potential issuers in the region. Furthermore, we will continue to provide funding through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" to encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong’s financing platform to raise sustainable funding. We will also step up promotional efforts to encourage more governments, entities, and corporates from the Mainland and other regions to raise green funding in Hong Kong. Meanwhile, we will continue to catalyse and support innovative sustainable finance, including providing grants to prospective digital green bond issuers through the Digital Bond Grant Scheme. Despite the growing market demand for high-quality sustainability disclosures by entities and corporates, different entities vary in their ability and preparedness to make such disclosures, and some may require additional guidelines and support. In light of this, the HKMA will continue to work with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group to make sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For instance, we will continue to provide banks and their customers with a wider range of climate disclosure-related tools, including user-friendly sustainability disclosure templates and supporting tools; explore how to leverage tech to further enhance the ease of use of existing resources; and collaborate with major local industry organisations to provide training needed by the sector. The sustainable finance market is evolving rapidly, requiring an expansion of the local talent pool and bridging knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and the region. Key tasks for the HKMA in 2025 include collaborating with the banking sector to develop professional-level training courses for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Enhanced Competency Framework", and identifying areas where the industry has further training needs through the upcoming "Future Banking Talent 2026–2030" study. Additionally, we plan to work with key stakeholders to strengthen the promotion of the government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" and review its applicability. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks to launch dedicated programmes in Asia, including conducting green finance studies, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted skills upgrading and training support, fostering community connections, facilitating access to potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidelines to assist banks in formulating roadmaps to develop green finance as a core business. As a responsible investor, the HKMA promises that the Exchange Fund portfolio will achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or sooner to support the headline economic transformation. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund’s investment through a pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment methodology, focusing primarily on the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that can bring positive climate outcomes. The HKMA is committed to setting an example in its own institutional sustainability efforts. In response to the accelerated timeline for achieving net-zero commitments announced in the "Action Plan", the HKMA will progressively integrate environmental and social factors into its strategies, risk assessments, and reporting at a pragmatic pace to continue driving institutional sustainability. Specifically, in 2025, we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring we focus on material topics. Furthermore, we will conduct energy audits and utilise tech solutions to evaluate the significant impact of climate risk on our offices and operations to enhance our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the "Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosures for Hong Kong" published by the government and are actively undertaking preparatory work to make disclosures in accordance with ISSB Standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to uphold its commitment to adhere to energy efficiency and conservation principles when selecting data centres for planned upgrading projects. We will also expand digital measures to foster sustainable development and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to facilitate paperless processes and waste reduction, and upgrading the overall digital experience for our staff, banks, and the general public.

Climate change impacts every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its related impacts. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking sector regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainable organisation, the HKMA contributes to fostering and accelerating the transformation towards net-zero in Hong Kong and across Asia. The HKMA has established a robust sustainable development governance framework to lead the formulation of its related strategies and policies; oversee the implementation of related actions; and ensure that sustainability factors are incorporated into the HKMA’s own operating processes and methodologies. In pursuit of good corporate governance, the HKMA has put in place a robust sustainable development governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and high transparency for its sustainability-related work. This governance framework ensures that sustainability factors are effectively integrated into the HKMA’s strategic planning and decision-making processes, and establishes effective mechanisms for monitoring and evaluating the progress and effectiveness of sustainability efforts. The HKMA’s sustainable development governance framework comprises: - The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which are responsible for overseeing the HKMA’s work, including its sustainability efforts, and making recommendations; - The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which is responsible for leading the HKMA’s headline environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategies and policies at the management level; - On responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office is responsible for coordinating and overseeing ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and - For other functional areas, relevant teams and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing relevant sustainability actions relating to banking and market developments as well as the HKMA’s own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the efforts of financial regulators, government bureaux, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the visible expansion in the scope of the HKMA’s various sustainability initiatives over the past few years, we established the Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across different functional areas of the HKMA. The Steering Committee: - Provides guidelines on the formulation of strategies, policies, and programmes relating to ESG-related matters across four functional areas: the banking sector, the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investments, and internal operations; - Oversees the implementation of ESG-related programmes by various functional departments of the HKMA; - Evaluates the HKMA’s performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG targets; and - Oversees external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with three Deputy Chief Executives serving as standing members. In addition, Executive Directors in charge of major functions related to green and sustainability matters will be invited to attend meetings of the Steering Committee to report on key outcomes of their work and future plans. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the Banking Department, Institutional Development and Operations Department, External Affairs Department, and the Exchange Fund Investment Office of the HKMA. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability actions, the HKMA co-initiated the establishment of the Steering Group with the SFC in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts for the financial sector to combat climate and environmental risks, thereby strengthening Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable financial centre in Asia and globally. For details of the Steering Group’s work, please refer to the chapter on “Strengthening the Development of the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem”.

Climate change may pose risks to the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening the ability of Hong Kong’s financial system to combat climate risk, while contributing to Hong Kong’s climate targets and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability- and climate-related issues in their day-to-day business operations, and therefore have to proactively manage climate risk. Meanwhile, banks play an important role in the financial system by channelling fund flows towards green and sustainable projects. As a regulator of the banking sector, the HKMA has placed particular emphasis on building banks’ capacity to address and manage climate risk, and accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. In October, the HKMA announced the Sustainable Finance Action Plan (“Action Plan”), setting out its vision to further consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a regional sustainable finance centre and support sustainable development in Asia and globally. The Action Plan comprises eight goals across four areas. To assist the industry in achieving the relevant banking policy goals, we have been undertaking the following work. All banks are committed to achieving net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or before, and net-zero financed emissions by 2050 or before. All banks are to increase transparency regarding climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared good practices on transition planning with the industry and launched an industry consultation on the draft Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-2 “Transition Planning”. The new module aims to provide guidelines on enhancing banks’ ability to address the net-zero transition and related risk management. Moreover, we are reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks’ capital adequacy levels and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with the aim of incorporating relevant factors proposed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee) on the effective management of climate-related financial risks into the assessment process, and encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks, including transition planning, to address climate risk. The HKMA has been working to align local sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, including the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) Standards and the Basel Committee’s Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analysing the latest developments in sustainability disclosure and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on the adoption of ISSB Standards. Fostering green and transition finance is key to implementing the Action Plan. In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (Taxonomy) to address industry concerns about greenwashing and help guide fund flows towards green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities under four sectors, aiming to align with the Common Ground Taxonomy as well as the taxonomies of Mainland China and the European Union, while incorporating relevant elements tailored to local circumstances. We have commenced Phase 2 work to expand the scope covered by the Taxonomy and are consulting a wide range of stakeholders to further facilitate green and sustainable financing. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks’ climate risk management and worked to support banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and combat climate change. The HKMA also completed all tasks under the two-year plan formulated in 2022 to integrate climate risk into the bank supervisory process. To foster banks’ capacity to manage climate risk, the HKMA shared good practices observed during thematic reviews and consultative meetings with the banking sector, which mainly include: - Establishing a sound governance framework with clearly defined responsibilities for the board and senior management; - Ensuring effective monitoring of key aspects of climate-related risk matters: (1) fostering and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) adopting appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) establishing a strong climate risk culture within the entity. In August, the HKMA held a Balanced Regulation Roundtable focusing on climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged opinions on various climate risk-related topics, including challenges faced by banks in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning, and finance. This roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and supported the HKMA’s work on climate risk supervision and other related areas. The HKMA launched a round of thematic reviews on banks’ climate risk management frameworks and practices, assessing their soundness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 “Climate Risk Management”. The thematic reviews covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress-tested scenarios. The HKMA held a second series of consultative meetings to assess the progress of a new batch of banks in implementing Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 “Climate Risk Management” and to understand the challenges they face. The consultative meetings also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and the issue of greenwashing. We provided feedback and guidelines based on banks’ specific circumstances to support their climate risk management efforts. The HKMA completed the second round of the Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST) for the banking sector in 2024, with participation from 21 retail banks and the Hong Kong branches of 25 international banking groups. Results suggest that under various scenarios, including assumptions where climate risk and macroeconomic downward shocks occur simultaneously, the Hong Kong banking sector continued to demonstrate strong resilience to withstand severe climate-related shocks. Compared to the CRST pilot exercise, participating banks significantly enhanced their ability to measure and assess climate risk. A report detailing the CRST results and good practices observed by the HKMA during the process was published in February 2025. Recognising the numerous challenges related to data and methodology that banks encounter in climate risk management, the HKMA has been undertaking various initiatives to promote the use of technology to address these challenges. To address the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risk assessment, the HKMA introduced a Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will upgrade the platform based on user feedback and by incorporating more local data. Furthermore, the HKMA is collaborating with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the broader financial services sector. During the year, we published practical application guides and two Regtech Adoption Case Briefs (in English), outlining technology solutions for environmental, social and governance (ESG) and sustainability assessments, as well as greenwashing risk management. We also hosted the third “FiNETech”, bringing together over 150 financial institutions and tech firms to explore co-operation in green fintech. Understanding that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and studies to strengthen current monitoring efforts. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks and includes analysis of climate-related risks in various Financial Stability Reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Workstream under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helps further enrich climate scenarios, assisting central banks and regulators in understanding the impact of climate change on the macroeconomic and macro-financial environment. In November, the NGFS released the fifth vintage of long-term climate macro-financial scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessments. As a member of the Financial Stability Board’s Transition Planning Working Group, the HKMA participated in analysing the interplay between transition planning of financial and non-financial corporates and financial stability, enabling policymakers to examine climate-related financial vulnerabilities from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA published the “Practical Guide on Green Technology Adoption for Banks” (in English), providing financial institutions with best practices on using green technology to facilitate their net-zero transition. On the research front, the HKMA conducted various applied research projects examining the impact of climate change on the financial sector and the overall economy. Research topics included the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in withstanding monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial sector in transitioning to a low-carbon economy. These research findings not only enhance our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability but also provide valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, aiding in policy formulation. Domestically, these studies help strengthen the HKMA’s ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. Research findings are also shared with a broad range of stakeholders through international forums and various channels such as HKMA Research Memoranda. The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research, the research arm of the Hong Kong Academy of Finance, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provides evidence suggesting that low-emission firms can benefit significantly from carbon pricing, highlighting its role in increasing benefits by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission firms. The study was featured in the Institute’s “Insights from Monetary Research” and shared with local and international scholars and policy researchers. The HKMA’s Liquidity Facilities Framework is a collateralised standby liquidity facility that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations when assessing eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risk and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through this engagement, we help foster policy dialogue on combating climate change and its impact on financial stability at international and regional levels, drawing lessons to strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong’s financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading regional green and sustainable finance hub, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As set out in the HKMA’s “Sustainable Finance Action Plan” (“Action Plan”), the HKMA strives to upgrade the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by fostering net-zero financing and promoting more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to establishing Hong Kong as a preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers in the region and globally, supporting technological innovation in the green segment of the financial market, enhancing sustainable disclosure by the industry, expanding the local green talent pool, and addressing knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. Establishing Hong Kong as a preferred sustainable financing platform in the region and globally Catalysing sustainable finance innovation Supporting high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure Bridging talent and knowledge gaps in regional sustainable finance To demonstrate the Government’s determination to combat climate change, promote green finance, and develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government introduced the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds totalling approximately US$28 billion equivalent, sold to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds raised have been allocated to over 110 government green projects, covering areas such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency, and energy conservation. We have seized every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currencies, tenors, and distribution channels, laying the foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the impact of the programme and further consolidate Hong Kong’s status as a green and sustainable finance hub, the scope of the programme was expanded to cover sustainable projects, and it was renamed the “Government Sustainable Bond Programme” (Sustainable Bond Programme). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Programme, the Government publishes an annual Green Bond Report detailing the allocation of proceeds raised from green bonds and their expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing approximately US$3 billion equivalent of institutional green bonds under the Sustainable Bond Programme. This triple-currency offering covered renminbi, US dollar, and Euro bonds with different tenors. These bonds attracted a diverse range of investors and were met with strong subscription, recording over US$15 billion equivalent in orders. Notably, the 20-year and 30-year renminbi green bonds marked the Government’s initial green bond issuance at these tenors, representing the longest-dated renminbi bonds issued by the Government to date. They provide a new baseline for the market and further demonstrate the catalytic role of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also further enrich the choice of offshore renminbi investment products in Hong Kong. Moreover, the enthusiastic response from global investors to the Government’s green bond offerings reflects their recognition of Hong Kong’s commitment to fostering green and sustainable development. To encourage more regional borrowers to use Hong Kong’s financing platform to raise funds for sustainable development, the HKMA continued to implement the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme, which was introduced in May 2021 to provide grants for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The scheme has been well received by the industry. By end-2024, grants had been approved for around 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong with a total amount exceeding US$140 billion. The scheme was extended by three years to 2027 in May 2024, with its coverage expanded to include transition bonds and loans. The extension and expansion of the scheme aim to encourage borrowers in relevant industries in the region to utilise Hong Kong’s transition financing platform for gradual decarbonisation. - Grants approved for around 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong with a total amount exceeding US$140 billion (as at end-2024) - Extended by three years to 2027, with coverage expanded to transition finance instruments Meanwhile, the HKMA has actively promoted Hong Kong’s sustainable financing platform, achieving positive results. Notably, the Shenzhen Municipal People’s Government issued offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong for the fourth time in August, totalling RMB 7 billion, including RMB 2.7 billion in green bonds, RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds, and RMB 900 million in social responsibility bonds. In September, the People’s Government of Guangdong Province issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, totalling RMB 5 billion, including RMB 1.5 billion in green bonds. In October, the People’s Government of Hainan Province also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, totalling RMB 3 billion, including RMB 1 billion in blue bonds and RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds. These bond issuance activities have repeatedly highlighted Hong Kong’s unique role in facilitating green and sustainable fund flows between the Mainland and the rest of the world. With these various measures, Hong Kong has consolidated its position as the premier platform for sustainable financing in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, Hong Kong remained the largest hub for arranging international green and sustainable bonds in Asia in 2024, with related bonds arranged through Hong Kong reaching a total amount of US$43.1 billion, accounting for 45% of the regional total. To catalyse sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two landmark tokenised green bonds in 2023 and 2024, which were the first tokenised government green bonds globally and the first multi-currency digital bonds globally, respectively. These offerings demonstrate the Government’s support for market participants in the region to apply asset digitalisation and innovative technologies in the green and sustainable finance space. The HKMA also introduced the Digital Bond Grant Scheme in November to foster digital bond issuance in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting innovative development in Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance market. The Working Group on Sustainability Disclosure under the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group) has been working on the adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) in Hong Kong. In December 2024, the Government published the Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure for Hong Kong, providing a clear path for large publicly accountable entities to fully adopt the ISSB Standards no later than 2028. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to provide support to entities at different stages of preparedness to achieve high-quality sustainable disclosure, making sustainable disclosure more accessible and inclusive. Notably, we continue to encourage the use of the “Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies” (Questionnaire), launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Questionnaire provides user-friendly disclosure templates to facilitate sustainable disclosure by firms, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024 to ease online completion by firms (see QR code below). The HKMA is upgrading the Questionnaire based on industry feedback and latest international developments to make it more user-friendly. Concrete measures include identifying core questions within the Questionnaire and providing common usage scenarios. In addition, we strive to enhance the compatibility of the Questionnaire with other supporting tools available on the Steering Group’s website. For more information on the Questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage. Leading by example, the HKMA demonstrates its commitment by making high-quality sustainable disclosures in its Sustainability Report in accordance with the latest global standards. The report contains rich content on the HKMA’s climate-related operational risks, as well as plans and implementation progress towards achieving climate targets. For details on sustainability disclosures regarding our own operations, please refer to the chapter “A Sustainable HKMA”. Given the rapidly evolving sustainable finance market, the HKMA is strengthening skills training for the banking sector and fostering knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders to bridge knowledge and talent gaps. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners in sustainable finance, the HKMA, in conjunction with the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB), launched the Foundation Level of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the Enhanced Competency Framework in July 2023. This module aims to help professionals in the banking sector acquire knowledge in green and sustainable finance more effectively and develop relevant professional competencies, covering four major functional areas: (1) Green and Sustainable Finance Products and Services; (2) Sustainable/Climate Risk Management; (3) Sustainable Disclosure and Reporting; and (4) Sustainable Strategies, Compliance, and Controls. Furthermore, the Professional Level of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module, targeting mid-to-senior level banking practitioners responsible for related work, was also launched in November. To provide necessary training for banking practitioners, the HKIB, as the administering body of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module, launched the Foundation Level training course for the module in May. Following the launch of the Professional Level in November, the HKMA will collaborate with the banking sector in 2025 to develop the Professional Level training course. To understand further skills and training needs of the banking sector, the HKMA is currently collaborating with the banking sector on the “Future Banking Talent 2026–2030” study, aiming to publish the findings in 2025. This joint study follows up on the “Future Banking Talent 2021–2025” paper published in June 2020. The findings of this follow-up study will serve as an important reference for the industry to formulate and adjust talent training strategies and actions, supporting the sustainable development of the banking sector. Through collaboration with the Steering Group, the HKMA continues to assist in implementing the Government-funded Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme, which subsidises practitioners, graduates, and students to receive sustainable finance-related training. As at December 2024, a total of 85 international and local programmes were registered as eligible training courses under the scheme, and over 5,700 reimbursement applications had been approved. The Government announced in the 2025-26 Budget that the scheme will be extended to 2028. The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to foster skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international co-operation. As a founding member of the Coalition for Sustainable Investing Capacity Building (CASI), the HKMA’s Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-hosted a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, focusing on global sustainable finance markets, policy frameworks, and innovative derivative instruments. In addition, the HKMA supported the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) in establishing a chapter in Hong Kong in October, and will leverage GFANZ’s network and expertise to strengthen skills training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA plays an active leading role in fostering the development of green and sustainable finance. Drawing on its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can be mutually reinforcing, the HKMA adheres to responsible investment principles in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritises sustainable assets, and requires its external investment managers to actively exercise ownership. The HKMA invests prudently in accordance with the principle of "Capital Preservation First, Long-term Growth Second", believing that paying full attention to environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate related investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable worth of investments. As a committed signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is dedicated to advancing its responsible investment efforts. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, aiming to enhance the resilience of the Exchange Fund and strive for better risk-adjusted long-term return. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring various derivative to channel capital into sustainable investment across different asset classes (Chart 1). Leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to fostering the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA published the "HKMA ESG Expectations" and made the documents available to investment partners through annual ESG workshops and the HKMA website. We work with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to jointly develop industry practice standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment by the financial sector and central banks. Through these co-operation efforts, we are committed to fostering a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. In October, the HKMA announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), articulating its commitment to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund "portfolio" by 2050 or sooner, and mobilising partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, further consolidating its commitment to investing in a sustainable future. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, has established the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The primary guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to balance the implementation of responsible investment with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring ESG and climate-related risks associated with Exchange Fund investment projects. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors relevant implementation through regular meeting reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Chart 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and monitoring various ESG initiatives of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Motions and work progress discussed at quarterly meetings of the ESG Committee are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Moreover, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets regularly to provide guidelines on ESG policy and actions for different functions of the HKMA, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG target. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with various teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office on integrating ESG factors, and assists senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing ESG, especially climate-related, risks and opportunities across various investment projects: - Open Markets Investment – The Credit, Regulation and Monitoring Committee, composed of senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with reference to opinions from the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG status of fixed income portfolios through regular reporting by the Risk Management and Compliance Department. In addition, the Sustainable Investment Team participates in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external investment managers for equity portfolios from an ESG perspective (for details, please refer to the section "Promoting Active Ownership" under "Risk Management" on page 39). - Private Market Investment – The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams for each proposed investment. The HKMA understands that physical and transition risks arising from climate change, as well as related opportunities, may affect the long-term financial performance of Exchange Fund investment projects. The United Nations Environment Programme’s "2024 Emissions Gap Report" projects that unless there is rapid and large-scale global mobilisation to reduce GHG emission, the global average temperature will increase by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Uncertainties regarding policy changes, technology development and behavioural shifts in response to rising temperatures may heighten transition risks, lead to increased market volatility and affect asset valuation. Meanwhile, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also bring additional risks of physical damage and financial losses to investment projects. Amidst these challenges, governments and sectors turning to sustainable solutions also create investment opportunities with potentially attractive long-term outlook in low-carbon solutions, emerging tech and sustainable infrastructure. The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors when integrating ESG factors. The HKMA has set a target for the Exchange Fund "portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or sooner, and continues to advance this goal through an orderly three-pronged methodology (see Chart 3). The HKMA announced the "Action Plan" in 2024, which consolidates the Exchange Fund's commitments and efforts related to climate transition (see Chart 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the HKMA favours proactive engagement over exclusion or divestment from investable projects. Investing in a Sustainable Future Achieving Net-Zero Emissions for the Exchange Fund "Portfolio" by 2050 or Sooner - Actively expanding the scope and offerings of sustainable investments, especially climate transition-themed investments in public and private markets - Integrating ESG factors into every investment decision, with particular focus on climate change and transition outlook considerations - Formulating clear ESG expectations aligned with international standards and best practices, and requiring all external investment managers, investee firms and counterparties to comply - Committing to reducing the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund equity portfolio by 67% from 2017 levels by 2030 or sooner Supporting Regional Transition through Investment - Continuing engagement with external investment managers to enhance enhancements in transition-driving investment opportunities - Continuing to identify and prioritise quality investment opportunities that foster transition in Asia and bring positive impact globally First, maintaining a diverse and sound portfolio is critical to achieving the primary investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially impacting investment return and risk. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in corporates undergoing transition, equipped with advanced technology and sound governance to address evolving global climate trends, including those in high-emission sectors. Second, combating climate change requires the transition of core "brown" sectors. Merely excluding related investment projects or divesting does not help resolve carbon emission issues. Instead, the HKMA supports these sectors by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising ownership, driving their transition to sustainable and low-carbon operating practices, thereby bringing beneficial changes to themselves and the world. The net-zero investment approach has evolved from favouring green or low-carbon assets to covering assets with credible transition outlook, to drive full decarbonisation of the headline economy. As a global asset owner, the HKMA understands that the long-term resilience of a portfolio relies not only on the portfolio's own adjustments but also on broad economic transition. Despite the absence of a perfect single solution, the HKMA enhanced its responsible investment strategies in 2024, adopting a full and diverse approach to drive transition while supporting both the Exchange Fund and global net-zero targets. This strategy combines top-down and bottom-up derivative, including integrating ESG factors and stewardship into fundamental analysis, portfolio decarbonisation tilting, and thematic investment targeting various assets aligned with net-zero pathways. In public markets, this may involve tilting the portfolio towards ESG leaders or climate solution providers, complemented by stewardship to drive corporate transition. In private markets, greater focus may be placed on transition-facilitating investment projects. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to identify investment opportunities that foster climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund portfolio. Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for over 10% of the Exchange Fund "portfolio", with financial performance comparable to relevant portfolio benchmarks (Chart 5). - Public Market Investment – The HKMA launched an active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and extended the application of customised low-carbon equity indices to two other portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continues to seek Green, Social and Sustainability (GSS) bonds that offer competitive return while financing sustainable projects (see the section "Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds" for relevant case studies). - Private Market Investment – The HKMA is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio to capture investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and professional expertise, the HKMA actively identifies and evaluates investment opportunities that accelerate energy transition, including through establishing strategic partnerships with multinational organisations (see the section "Joining Forces to Combat Climate Challenges in Asia and Beyond" for examples). - Passive portfolios benchmarked against ESG indices - Customised decarbonisation strategies for passive and active quantitative portfolios with non-ESG index benchmarks - Governance-themed active portfolios - Active ESG portfolios themed on sustainability and climate transition - Projects with sustainable features, such as renewable energy infrastructure, and green-certified buildings and warehouses - Funds themed on energy transition and decarbonisation in the Global, Asia and Global South - Green, Social and Sustainability bonds - A green bond fund managed by an international organisation - The "Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program" (MCPP), managed by the International Finance Corporation, focusing on sustainable projects in emerging markets - The "MCPP One Planet" initiative, providing Paris Agreement-aligned climate-related investments in emerging markets The HKMA invested in green bonds issued by a quasi-official entity. Proceeds raised from the green bonds were allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading outdated equipment at several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrades cover enhancements to monitoring and control systems and pump performance to yield positive environmental benefits from wastewater management, waste reduction and recycling processes. In addition to continuous wastewater and sludge treatment, these facilities compost or reuse dewatered sludge to produce fertiliser, charcoal, cement and other construction materials, achieving a sludge recycling rate of up to 100%. These facilities also utilise gas generated during sludge treatment to power boilers and generate electricity. The HKMA invested in green bonds issued by a multilateral development bank. The bonds financed multiple projects, including the rehabilitation of a national canal system. As one of the country's largest irrigation systems, the canal aims to divert excess water from rivers to arid regions. The project primarily aims to rehabilitate deteriorating canal linings to prevent seepage, conserve water, improve water efficiency and reclaim flooded areas. Furthermore, the project provides skills training for local stakeholders to promote the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation techniques such as micro-irrigation and sustainable farming methods.

The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable entity. A key focus of the HKMA’s work in 2024 to fulfill this promise was the plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net-zero GHG emissions from its corporate operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of the original target, consistent with the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan". In addition to fostering environmental sustainability, the HKMA has also made promises to promote staff training and physical and mental well-being, and strives to promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is the major decision-making body for various corporate sustainability actions. To demonstrate the HKMA’s commitment to combat climate change, the Steering Committee approved in October 2024 a new target for the HKMA to achieve net-zero GHG emissions from its corporate operations by 2030 or earlier, as part of the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"). At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Corporate Development and Operations) provided guidelines on the implementation arrangement of sustainability actions regarding corporate operations, staff well-being, and social connection, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Administration Division serves as the coordinator and central hub for executing, communicating, and reporting on corporate sustainability actions. The Green Office Task Force and Volunteer Service Team, composed of staff from various operating departments, provide an additional layer of support; the former is a platform for brainstorming suggestions on how to create a green working environment, while the latter aims to foster a culture of staff participation in volunteer activities. In recognition of the HKMA’s dedication to caring for the environment, staff, and the community at large, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years+ Caring Organisation" logo for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA’s sustainability strategies continue to adopt a structure comprising three pillars: Environment, Staff, and Social Responsibility. - Focusing on decarbonisation and digitalising of the HKMA’s day-to-day operations, aiming to achieve net-zero emissions by 2030 or earlier - Adopting green procurement requirements in accordance with government guidelines - Promoting greener operating practices to the finance sector and the wider community - Building a positive workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA’s strategic objectives - Creating a collaborative, caring, and inclusive work environment that values diversity and strengthens staff sense of belonging - Providing a quality work environment to foster healthier lifestyles - Cultivating a socially responsible culture - Integrating social considerations into procurement processes and supply chains management - Fostering financial inclusion and enhancing public financial literacy through consumer education activities The HKMA pays particular interest to climate change and leads by example. In October 2024, the HKMA announced plans to bring forward the target date for achieving net-zero GHG emissions from its own corporate operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of its previous promises, as part of the "Action Plan". The HKMA has made amendments to its roadmap towards net-zero transformation, focusing on responsibly managing the impact of day-to-day operations on the environment, with a focus on reducing carbon emissions, energy conservation, paper reduction, and waste recycling, while making full use of improvements in the fuel mix for power generation by local power companies. Moreover, the HKMA has established a digital working environment to increase efficiency and simultaneously reduce its carbon footprint. Furthermore, the HKMA understands the importance of fostering a sustainability culture, and therefore encourages staff to actively adopt practices conducive to sustainable development through continuous promotional programmes and activities. Under the primary 2030 net-zero target, the HKMA has been examining the adoption of carbon insetting derivative within its own value chain to mitigate emissions, and low-carbon procurement wherever possible. In this regard, since 2023, the HKMA has fully offset carbon emissions from air travel through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel and participation in carbon offsetting programmes. The HKMA will expand its carbon insetting and carbon offsetting programmes to cover all remaining major carbon emissions. In addition to the above environmental commitments regarding actual operations, the HKMA continues to foster the low-carbon transformation of the market, ranging from introducing electronic documents submission and processing procedures to fostering electronic payments and collecting coins back into circulation. The remainder of this chapter details the HKMA’s strategies in leading environmental protection, as well as fostering staff well-being and social care. Under the HKMA’s overall corporate risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing potential risks and threats confronted with by the HKMA in its day-to-day operations, including those arising from climate change. To more effectively evaluate the impact that climate change may bring to operations, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and reviewed actual and potential impacts. To combat climate-related risks and ensure continued operations, the HKMA offices are designed incorporating various actions to mitigate potential physical hazards, fire, and other emergencies. Moreover, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans, incorporating full measures covering not only offices but also communications and computer facilities. The HKMA regularly holds evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure staff remain prepared to execute contingency measures at any time. The HKMA has also been monitoring transition risks by tracking GHG emissions generated from its own operations, waste generation, as well as energy consumption and paper usage. The HKMA’s latest climate target is to achieve net-zero GHG emissions for Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 related to corporate operations by 2030 or earlier. These targets were developed referencing the methodology of the Science Based Targets initiative. The HKMA uses the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to calculate and report corporate emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the simplicity of its operations, the HKMA’s major GHG emissions are Scope 2 indirect GHG emissions resulting from electricity generation via fossil fuel consumption. Due to the lack of individual supplier dataset, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach to estimate major Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital products) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills and staff air travel and commuting. Detailed calculated results for 2023 and 2024 are set out in the "Performance Summary" on page 50. Performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and baseline of the verification are set out in the attached "Verification Statement" at the end of this report. The HKMA leads by example, adhering to the same climate-related standards expected of the banks it regulates and the financial system it monitors. As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA started replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this work in 2025 to achieve full green mobility. The HKMA continues to integrate environmental factors into office design, operations, and maintenance. Specifically, in various renovation projects in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and decoration materials or traded in old items for new ones to reduce waste. To enhance overall energy benefits, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and conservation measures for offices and data centres, and adopted modular design uninterruptible power supply systems in the 2024 data centre facility upgrading project, further optimising the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus certified data centres. This design allows flexible capacity expansion, increases operating efficiency under partial load, and features advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping to reduce overall energy consumption. The HKMA enhances internal virtual collaboration through digital workplaces, coupled with streamlined workflows, effectively reducing paper usage. Moreover, referencing manufacturers' software update cycles, the HKMA extends the service life of mobile and desktop devices, extending the secure usage period of the devices. To reduce waste generated from offices, the HKMA follows the "4R" principles: refuse, reduce, reuse, and recycle, and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. Recycling bins for different materials are placed at various convenient locations in the office. To increase recycling rates, the HKMA added recycling bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit mesh bags in 2024. Moreover, since November 2022, the HKMA has sent collected food waste to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA participated in the Environmental Protection Department's "Event Waste Reduction Charter", making promises to take actions to reduce waste generated from various events. The HKMA continues to prioritise the procurement of goods meeting the environmental specifications of the Government's "Green Procurement List", particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to carefully plan trips, such as combining multiple journeys when attending overseas events where possible. At the corporate level, the HKMA has purchased sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing annual air travel carbon emissions by approximately 10%. Additionally, the HKMA participates in Gold Standard certified carbon offsetting programmes to offset remaining air travel carbon emissions; these programmes focus on renewable energy production and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged various learning activities for staff, such as seminars and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance staff understanding of environmental sustainability issues. From Earth Day on April 22, 2024, throughout May, the HKMA held its inaugural "HKMA Green Month" under the theme "Think Green, Live Green, Work Green". This was a prime opportunity to demonstrate the HKMA’s commitment and drivers to practicing environmental sustainability in internal operations. Activities included the "Sustainability BINGO Scorecard" encouraging staff to practice green living, the "Save the Earth" quiz, and a "Kokedama" indoor plant workshop originating from Japan; waste audit results were shared, and operators of community recycling centres introduced best practices in recycling. To sustain the momentum of "Green Month", the HKMA launched a recycling campaign lasting about six months in October, highlighting responsible waste disposal and reminding staff that pooling small changes in personal habits can significantly improve overall corporate recycling performance. A highlight of the campaign was the launch of the "Green 'Fit' Action" video featuring senior executives sharing recycling tips. The campaign also introduced a range of screensavers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles, and e-alerts to remind staff to lead by example in waste reduction and increased recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff survey to understand their awareness of sustainable development and collect opinions on proposed green office actions. Survey results will help formulate future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies. As the central banking institution of Hong Kong, the HKMA sees itself as a key facilitator of change and is therefore committed to leading accelerated low-carbon transformation and fostering sustainable operating practices in the finance sector and society at large. The HKMA has introduced various actions to enhance the efficiency of external processes. Following the successful introduction of the "Common Data Submission Platform" in 2023, the HKMA expanded the platform's service scope in 2024 to cover non-bank entities, such as stored value payment tool operators, to ease their submission of certain regulatory information. Expanding the platform's service scope aims to further streamline the submission process for reporting entities, providing a smoother experience for all users, while strengthening the HKMA’s commitment to sustainable development. Other new measures introduced in 2024 include SurveyTool, which enables banks to respond to HKMA surveys via a simplified submission process, and the Intelligent Information and Documents Management System, a central platform providing users with advanced search and bank-related documents functions.

Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency has undertaken an independent verification of the environmental dataset (the “Dataset”) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (“HKMA”). The Dataset includes total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste disposed of at landfills and recyclable waste), and GHG emissions from air travel for 2024, along with their respective intensities. Moreover, the Dataset also includes Scope 3 GHG emissions arising from purchased goods and services, capital products, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste disposed of at landfills and recyclable waste), and staff commuting for 2023 and 2024, together with their corresponding intensities. The HKMA’s GHG emission data were compiled based on the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (“GHG Protocol”) jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covers a total of six office and warehouse assets, comprising five offices located at: 1) Two International Finance Centre; 2) Hopewell Centre; 3) Pacific Place Phase One; 4) Kowloon Trading Hub; and 5) Global Trade Square; and a warehouse at 6) Lok Sing Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the Dataset and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanisms. Within the verification scope, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency examined representative data selected from the six assets and supporting evidence. This verification engagement was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information,” issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were specifically designed to form opinions and conclusions to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification processes were established based on the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification processes tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing the selected sample data back to their sources, and also reviewed the underlying processes for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and performed reliability testing. The verification processes also included verifying domestic data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with proxies responsible for preparing the data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. Relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of the information. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team has not participated in the data preparation processes. Based on the results of this verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the Dataset and concludes that: - The Dataset is materially accurate and reliable; - The HKMA’s headline data collection mechanisms are strong. Sham Siu Yan Audit Manager Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2025
